result.title: Efficient Video Retrieval Augmented Generation via Token Allocation
result.summary: Efficient long-video understanding requires identifying relevant evidence while minimizing the tokens processed by vision-language models (VLMs). Existing video retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) methods rely on frame selection and token compression, but overlook how much each additional token is worth. We introduce Lembas, a plug-and-play framework that formulates video RAG as a token allocation problem over frames and subtitles under a shared budget. Our key insight is that the value of a token diminishes within each item and decreases further as similar evidence receives more tokens. Lembas captures both effects in a single objective and solves it with an efficient iterative water-filling algorithm that has a provable convergence guarantee. For multi-turn conversations, Lembas reuses the tokens processed in earlier turns and refines relevance with the VLM's attention at no extra cost. Our evaluations show that Lembas improves accuracy by up to 7.2 percentage points over state-of-the-art baselines at comparable compute. On multi-turn video understanding, Lembas achieves up to 1.5 percentage points higher accuracy with 1.7-17.3x fewer TFLOPs.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Lembas，把视频 RAG 建模为帧与字幕在共享预算下的 token 分配问题，用带收敛保证的迭代注水算法求解，并在多轮对话中复用已处理 token、借 VLM 注意力免费细化相关性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「token 边际价值随同一项内递减、相似证据越多越贬值」的目标直接对应 LVR 关注的视觉证据筛选与计算预算分配，可供核查；但优化的是输入 token 选择而非 latent 推理状态的生成与停止决策。
